_note: docs/v7/phase1-nft-pooled.md §1-§2: the five launch collections (docs/v7/phase1-nft.md §9 D1) as DeployStack takes them: ETCH_STACK_KIND=nft with ETCH_NFT_COLLECTIONS / _NAMES / _SYMBOLS / _SLUGS and ETCH_NFT_NORMAL_RAISES / _EARLY_RAISES / _CONV_BPS_LIST / _RESERVE_BPS_LIST as comma lists in this order; scripts/golive-dryrun.sh builds them from this file. Unnamed values take the frog stack's defaults: normalRaise 5 ETH, earlyRaise 8 ETH, earlyUntilEth 2 ETH, maxRaise 30 ETH, convBps 300, reserveBps 2500. BAYC is J1 as the operator decided it on 2026-09-27: 10 ETH (normal = early, the CurveFactory ceiling), convBps 1000, reserveBps 0. At the 6.79 floor one graduation converts 1.137 units, so it buys one ape alone; that holds while the floor at its graduation is at most 7.35 ETH (+8.26 %; above it BAYC pools two graduations per ape), and a graduation at 6.79 is still advanced and bought after a floor rise to 7.35 ETH (+8.32 %, the canister's advance gate: Relay's estimated 0.5 %, the floor + 1 % and 0.003 ETH). So any rise of up to 8.26 % from 6.79, before or after the graduation, still buys one ape with one graduation. convBps 1000 is where those two edges meet (the exact optimum at 6.79 is 997, +8.29 %).

_bitcoin: The operator, 2026-10-09: ordinals launch WITH the Ethereum collections, not as the second wave docs/v8/ordinals-wave.md §3.5 recommended. Bitcoin Frogs (Ordinals Wallet slug bitcoin-frogs) is the canister's one Bitcoin wrapper, deployed in the SAME deploy-stack.sh run as the Ethereum collections (eleven since Identity MD joined, 2026-10-09) (the default kind with ETCH_NFT_COLLECTIONS: one stack file, ETCH_STACK_SLUG=bitcoin-frogs, ETCH_WRAPPER_NAME / _SYMBOL as here), over a listInscriptionsAuto listing (script/list-auto.sh: ETCH_LIST_NAME / _REF as here, ETCH_LIST_ROOT = membersRoot, the root of membersFile's 10,000 ids, deployments/launch/btc/README.md). CUSTODY (H2, docs/v5/launch-gates.md G7 stage 0): the wrapper keeps stage 0's 3 items / 10 ETH (custody_caps key btc:0x<wrapper>), the same at every step of `stages`. THE EXIT RULE (A4-L-1, outflow::exit_fits): every item in custody must leave within the timelock's 72 h less a day, i.e. two usable days at global_items a day: at the install's 24 a day, 48 items in all. The Ethereum items at steps 1 and 2 therefore drop by 3, taken from Azuki (17 -> 14), whose per-item headroom is the deepest (J7 22 at its 0.67 ETH floor, so 14 items are 9.4 ETH of its 15 ETH; the others stay at their option-(c) split): the pilot five 13 + 14 + 13 + 3 + 2 = 45, plus Frogs 3 = 48 = globalItems = 24 x 2, and each collection alone at most 14 <= 12 x 2. (The global already binds at 48 with the dormant five's 12 each, so min(sum, global) was 48 before the shave too; the shave keeps the pilot five plus Frogs inside the global, as option (c) had the pilot five alone.) Step 3, the caps back to J7 (caps only, global_items stays step 2's 31): the pilot five's J7 61 + Frogs 3 = 64 would need 32 a day, so its global is 62 = 31 x 2, the most that leaves in two days at 31; Azuki returns to 22 and Frogs stays at 3. PURCHASES: maxPurchaseWei 0.5 ETH is the canister's policy MAX_PURCHASE_WEI (ordinals-wave §1.4; Frogs' floor 0.12-0.18 ETH, an advance 1.03 x floor <= 0.19 ETH), named by set_purchase_limit(<frogs floorModule>, 500000000000000000) before the handover. frog_funding: Relay at max_fee_bps 400, no float first (ordinals-wave §2 R4; etch_autobuyer.did FrogFunding, bounds [50, 500], the default when null is 300 / false: relayconv.rs). The custody fee pool needs one usable entry of at least custodyFeePoolMinSats (golive-check --min-fee-pool-sats, the monitor's min_fee_pool_sats) and the float a one-time padding seed of about floatPaddingSeedSats (ordinals-wave R10), both before the first conversion. unisatKeyRequired: contents verify on two per-output providers only with UniSat's key (set_unisat_key after the install and after EVERY upgrade: ordinals-wave §3.3). The keeper posts the Bitcoin module's floor from the Ordinals Wallet book (KEEPER_OW_SLUGS=bitcoin-frogs=bitcoin-frogs); the runner's protected step reads owSlug (RUNNER_OW_SLUG) with membersFile (RUNNER_OW_MEMBERS), and its UniSat step unisatCollection (RUNNER_UNISAT_COLLECTION). golive-check --launch reads this block (the staged plan and the exit rule count btc:0x<wrapper>; the listing's root, the wrapper's labels, and with --canister the cap, the Bitcoin floor sink and its limit, UniSat among ord_providers(), the fee pool; with --install-arg the wrapper and frog_funding; with --monitor-config the Bitcoin canary).
_inscriptions: docs/v9/ordinals-collections.md (2026-10-10): the further Ordinals collections, rook_core Inscriptions listings 12-25 in THIS order (12-16 the first pass; 17-25 appended 2026-10-10 by operator decision, most liquid first: every collection the first pass dropped except Ordinal Punks), after Bitcoin Frogs (11); launch-params.mjs listingOrder(), rook-ceremony (listing_order_from_pilot, pins), site-config.mjs and the site list them from here. APPEND ONLY: a listing id that has a day-1 DBC config is never moved or reused. Ids 12-16 were chosen by market data of 2026-10-10 (each: >= 30 single-item sales across venues in 30 days in Ordinals Wallet's sales feed, >= 3 listings from >= 3 sellers on Ordinals Wallet's book, the canister's buy venue and floor feed, and a floor inside the purchase bounds: frogsol.rs MIN_PURCHASE_LAMPORTS 1 SOL .. RELAY_SOL_BTC_MAX_LAMPORTS 250 SOL); ids 17-25 were added by the operator without those gates, and none of them passes the wake check today. membersFile: the ids Ordinals Wallet (turbo /collection/<owSlug>/inscriptions) AND the on-chain source agree on (ordGallery: an ord gallery inscription; ordParent: the collection's parent inscription's children; ordGrandparent: the children of every child of that inscription, RSIC's ten sub-parents), ordered by inscription number (ops/solana/ordinals-members.mjs fetch; <file>.provenance.json records every source and what each alone had; `ordinals-members.mjs check` recomputes count and root). membersRoot: the same tree as Bitcoin Frogs' (keccak256(keccak256(id)) leaves in list order, sorted pairs, odd node up: rook_core hashing.rs, ops/src/frogmath.ts proofFor); proofs are 11-15 hashes, and 17 (544 B) for Runestone's 112,384 members, inside one Solana transaction (rook_core has no proof cap; the canister's hand-in takes at most 32). Price references as Frogs': owSlug (the keeper / runner book) and coingeckoId (the monitor's D8 reference); unisatCollection is null until it is confirmed with the UniSat key (the collection index needs it). custodyItems / custodyWei: Frogs' stage-0 cap (3 items, 10 ETH; at the 2026-10-10 floors 3 NodeMonkes are about 3.3 ETH). maxPurchaseLamports: the canister's per-collection purchase limit on the Solana home (set_purchase_limit on the collection's module; frogsol::check_limits), max(10 SOL = MAX_PURCHASE_LAMPORTS, about 1.5 x the 2026-10-10 Ordinals Wallet floor), at most the 250 SOL ceiling. WRAPPING WAITS: the canister operates ONE Inscriptions wrapper (Init.wrapper = Bitcoin Frogs; docs/v9/ordinals-collections.md §4): these five are listed, their modules registered and their day-1 DBC configs created with the others, but no floor is posted for them (no posted floor: no mint, no advance) until the canister's multi-listing change ships and each passes the wake check of §5 (its Ordinals Wallet book within the D8 20 % band of the CoinGecko floor). Their custody caps and purchase limits are named then, not at the install.
_dormancy: docs/v7/dormant-collections.md §3.2 and §11: the install argument's eth_nft.dormancy, exactly (golive-check --launch --canister holds it; its wake_desk is the stack file's wakeDesk). The limits AUTO-SCALE with the canister's own liquid cycles balance (§11): effective_max_active = min(max_active, floor((balance - reserve - 7 x idle) / (7 x active + exit))) with the scaling's numbers in B cycles (2.5 T a day per active collection and 0.3 T idle, the high end of §7; 7 days of runway; a reserve of 8 T, the canister's own scan floor, plus 3 T per awake collection for its exits, returns and owed work), and a wake that is not owed starts only if the balance after its one-time cost (1.5 T) still covers 7 days at one more awake. max_active 10 and wakes_per_day 12 are only the hard ceilings (governance, timelocked). A collection with a position (a unit, an item, a rental, a graduation, an advance or a float, anything open in the canister) is never put to sleep and counts against the limit; while the limit is exceeded no new wake starts, and an awake collection with nothing open sleeps at its next check. One backfill at a time; a wake that has not confirmed its floor in 12 h fails, and a collection that failed or went back to sleep waits a day before a wake that is not owed; three days with no position, or six hours after a wake when none ever came, sends a collection back to sleep; owed wakes (a deposit, a queued graduation) have one slot above effective_max_active, may use the runways but never the reserve, and back off after a timeout (DR-H-1, DR-H-2).
_wake: docs/v7/dormant-collections.md §3.3: the WakeDesk (DeployStack: ETCH_WAKE_BOND, ETCH_WAKE_WINDOW): a public wake request costs a 0.002 ETH bond (the operator, 2026-10-09; 0.003 before: one wake burns 0.5-1.5 T, about $0.70-$2, which 0.002 ETH still covers), back to the requester once a coin they launch on the collection after asking reaches its raise within seven days (plus a day's grace; not a floor-buys-only coin, one coin one bond: dormant-review DR-H-1, DR-L-5). Otherwise anyone closes it: to the protocol treasury if the canister posted the collection's floor since the request, back to the requester if it never did (DR-H-3). golive-check holds the stack's desk to these numbers.
_cycles: docs/v7/dormant-collections.md §11 (13-node subnet): the starting balance is sized for ONE active collection for 7 days plus the reserve, and the limits grow with top-ups. The burn and the reserve are the dormancy's scaling (one source of truth); freezeT is what the freezing threshold (90 days of the idle memory burn) keeps out of the liquid balance. golive-check --launch FAILs unless startT - freezeT gives effective_max_active >= 1 AND lets the first wake start (1.5 T + 7 x (2.5 + 0.3) T + 8 T + 3 T = 32.1 T liquid): 34 T, about US$46 at 1.35 $/T. The rest of the operator's $100 (about 40 T) stays in the cycles ledger for top-ups; each 20.5 T more keeps one more collection awake (plus 1.5 T for its wake). The monitor pages when fewer collections can be awake than hold positions (eth-capacity-short), under 7 days of burn, and under 12 T.
_canister: eth_nft.collections: max_purchase_wei is each collection's maxPurchaseWei (milady 2 ETH, azuki 2 ETH, mayc 2 ETH, pudgypenguins 4 ETH, bayc 8 ETH; at BAYC's convBps 1000 8 ETH covers the item cap 1.10 x 6.79 = 7.47 and a buy at the +8.26 % edge (7.35 x 1.05 = 7.72); a graduation at the 7.35 edge has an item cap of 8.09, and the canister advances min(item cap, 8 ETH) (floorsink::view), which still reaches Ethereum covering a floor up to 7.88); max_premium_bps 500 each. script/golive-check.sh --launch holds the factory targets, the module conversion and reserve, and (with --canister) max_purchase_wei against this file (audit 2026-09-27-nft round 2, D2-L-5)
_custody: J7, decided by the operator 2026-09-27 (docs/v7/phase1-nft-pooled.md §6): each Ethereum collection's stage-0 custody cap is custodyWei = 15 ETH (one item up to 15 ETH) and custodyItems = what fits 15 ETH at its floor of 2026-09-27 (15 / floor, rounded down: Milady 0.93 → 16, Azuki 0.67 → 22, MAYC 0.8735 → 17, Pudgy 3.353 → 4, BAYC 6.79 → 2), and there is no canister-wide total: the install's custody_caps names the global caps as the sum of the collections' (48 items at step 1 of `stages`, 61 after step 3; 75 ETH), which never binds before theirs (review round 7, A7-I-2) (custodycap.rs FIRST_EVM_*, first_global). A deposit counts at the module's accepted floor (review round 3 A3-L-4). Because holders must be able to take every item out within the timelock's 72 h less a day (outflow::exit_fits), 22 items need 11 deliveries a day per collection: the install's outflow_limits are per_collection_items 12 and global_items 24 (x4 stage 0, the most an install may start at), per_collection_mints 3, global_mints 6, global_value_wei 25 ETH (H3, the operator 2026-09-27: 10 ETH before), trip_factor 3. script/golive-check.sh --launch holds custodyItems and custodyWei per collection against the canister's custody_caps(), and that the total never binds. AMENDED by docs/v7/dormant-collections.md §6 (2026-09-29): with the allowlist's ten collections the global IS named and binds (`stages` globalItems / globalWei), and golive-check holds the canister's global to it.
_outflow: The install's outflow_limits as _custody states them (the operator, 2026-09-27; unchanged), as data so script/golive-check.sh --launch holds them (review round 4, A4-I-2) and checks the exit rule against the whole custody (A4-L-1): every item of every collection must be able to leave within the timelock's 72 h less a day. At these limits the custodyItems above (step 1 of the operator's option (c): 48 in all) fit exactly (48 can leave at 24 a day within the two usable days); J7's 61 would not, which is why they come only at step 3, after step 2 raises global_items to 31 (`stages`, fixes-round5.md §6; review round 6 A6-L-1 corrected this text, which still said 61). openseaSlug / coingeckoId are the D8 references of deployments/launch/monitor-nft.json, held against it by collection (A3-L-3); a collection with priceRefs ["opensea"] (Identity MD alone, the operator 2026-10-09) names no coingeckoId and its monitor entry price_refs ["opensea"].
_stage: which step of `stages` the canister is at: golive-check --launch holds the canister to this step's numbers (--stage overrides it for a step's own read)

stages.name: install
stages._when: the launch install (the pre-handover reinstall, or the first timelocked upgrade carrying this build): 48 items in all (the global cap binds: docs/v7/dormant-collections.md §6) at 12 / 24 a day; the pilot five 45 (Azuki 14, `_bitcoin`) and Bitcoin Frogs 3 fill the global exactly

stages.name: outflow raise
stages._when: proposed only after step 1 has executed and the handover is done; runs 72 h later. Its argument differs from step 1's in outflow_limits.global_items alone (golive-check --proposal --stage 2). Any other upgrade of the buyer executed in those 72 h makes it stale: queue it again

stages.name: caps back to J7
stages._when: after two clean weeks at step 2: its argument differs from step 2's in custody_caps alone: the item counts J7's (Azuki back to 22), Bitcoin Frogs unchanged at 3, the global item cap 62 (golive-check --proposal --stage 3; `_bitcoin`: the pilot five's J7 61 + 3 = 64 would need 32 a day, so the global is the most 31 a day lets out in two days)

_stages: docs/v7/dormant-collections.md §6: with ten collections listed the canister-wide item cap is named and BINDS (globalItems, globalWei), where J7 had it the sum: 48 items at steps 1-2 and 61 at step 3 (62 since Bitcoin Frogs joined the launch, `_bitcoin`), 75 ETH, so every item still leaves within the timelock's 72 h less a day (min(the collections' sum, the global) at global_items a day). Identity MD (2026-10-09, 8 items at every step) changes no global: the sums are 116 at steps 1-2 (the pilot five 45 + the dormant five 60 + Identity MD 8 + Bitcoin Frogs 3) and 192 at step 3 (61 + 120 + 8 + 3), still over the globals, so what can be held is min(116, 48) = 48 <= 2 x 24 = 48 at step 1, 48 <= 2 x 31 = 62 at step 2 and min(192, 62) = 62 <= 2 x 31 = 62 at step 3; its own 8 <= 2 x per_collection_items 12 = 24 at every step. Adding a collection to a binding global adds no item that can be held at once: it shares the 48 / 62. Only ACTIVE collections hold items (a collection sleeps only with none held), so at most max_active of them count toward it at once.
